narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To explain how an increase in supply and a decrease in demand leads to falling prices and subsequent driver protests.

units.meaning: SUPPLY increases from its minimum relative value at the left endpoint to its maximum relative value at the right endpoint.

basis.note: SUPPLY starts at the minimum of the relative scale.
SUPPLY ends at the maximum of the relative scale.

accepted_routes: Supply rises from 0 to 1 on the relative scale.
Supply line climbs from its lowest to its highest relative value.
Supply increases steadily across the clip.
Supply goes from minimum to maximum relative value.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The SUPPLY series must be visibly increasing from the leftmost to the rightmost sampled point, starting at the bottom of the relative scale and ending at the top.
units.reviewer_question: Is the overall upward SUPPLY trend required, or are the endpoints enough?

units.meaning: DEMAND decreases from its maximum relative value at the left endpoint to its minimum relative value at the right endpoint.

basis.note: DEMAND starts at the maximum of the relative scale.
DEMAND ends at the minimum of the relative scale.

accepted_routes: Demand falls from 1 down to 0 on the relative scale.
Demand line descends from its highest to its lowest relative value.
Demand decreases steadily across the clip.
Demand goes from maximum to minimum relative value.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The DEMAND series must be visibly decreasing from the leftmost to the rightmost sampled point, starting at the top of the relative scale and ending at the bottom.
units.reviewer_question: Is the overall downward DEMAND trend required, or are the endpoints enough?

units.meaning: The two series move in opposite directions: SUPPLY increases while DEMAND decreases over the same x_px range.

basis.note: SUPPLY begins at the bottom.
SUPPLY ends at the top.
DEMAND begins at the top.
DEMAND ends at the bottom.

accepted_routes: Supply and demand move in opposite directions.
Supply rises while demand falls.
The two lines diverge.
One line goes up as the other goes down.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The SUPPLY and DEMAND series must have opposite slopes across the clip: SUPPLY visibly rising while DEMAND visibly falling.
units.temporal_anchor: when this line goes up and this one goes down
units.reviewer_question: Must the video show the opposite movement simultaneously, or can it establish the two directions in separate beats?

units.meaning: The relative ordering of the two series flips: DEMAND starts above SUPPLY and ends below SUPPLY; the first sampled point where SUPPLY exceeds DEMAND is x_px=881.5 (SUPPLY 0.5170, DEMAND 0.4830), after SUPPLY was below DEMAND at x_px=853.3 (SUPPLY 0.4789, DEMAND 0.5211).

basis.note: DEMAND is above SUPPLY at the start.
SUPPLY is below DEMAND at the start.
SUPPLY is still below DEMAND here.
DEMAND is still above SUPPLY here.
SUPPLY first exceeds DEMAND at this sampled point.
DEMAND first falls below SUPPLY at this sampled point.
SUPPLY is above DEMAND at the end.
DEMAND is below SUPPLY at the end.

accepted_routes: Supply overtakes demand around the middle of the clip.
Demand is higher than supply at the start, but supply is higher at the end.
The lines cross between the x_px=853.3 and x_px=881.5 samples.
The ordering flips from demand>supply to supply>demand.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show DEMAND above SUPPLY early on and SUPPLY above DEMAND later, including a visible crossing or change in relative order between the x_px=853.3 and x_px=881.5 samples.
units.temporal_anchor: when this line goes up and this one goes down
units.reviewer_question: Is the crossing/ordering flip required, or is it enough to show SUPPLY rising and DEMAND falling?

units.meaning: At the left endpoint, DEMAND is at its maximum relative value 1.0000 while SUPPLY is at its minimum 0.0000; at the right endpoint, SUPPLY is at its maximum 1.0000 while DEMAND is at its minimum 0.0000.

basis.note: SUPPLY is at the bottom at the start.
DEMAND is at the top at the start.
SUPPLY is at the top at the end.
DEMAND is at the bottom at the end.

accepted_routes: Demand starts at the top and supply at the bottom, then they swap.
At the beginning demand is highest and supply lowest; at the end supply is highest and demand lowest.
The start and end are mirror opposites on the relative scale.
The two series exchange their relative extreme positions.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The leftmost sampled position must show DEMAND at the maximum and SUPPLY at the minimum; the rightmost sampled position must show SUPPLY at the maximum and DEMAND at the minimum.
units.temporal_anchor: when this line goes up and this one goes down
units.reviewer_question: Is an explicit start/end extreme comparison needed, or do the trend lines alone suffice?

optional_valid: The narration may mention falling prices and driver protests as contextual consequences, but the table contains no price or protest data. If used, keep them verbal/contextual rather than table-derived.
unsupported_to_avoid: Any numeric price value or price change, since the table has no price column.
Any claim that supply and demand caused prices to fall or drivers to protest, because the table only contains relative supply and demand series.
Percentages, counts, or absolute quantities for SUPPLY or DEMAND, since their unit is relative and values are 0-1 normalizations.
Treating relative_value as a percentage (e.g., 'demand falls 100%') instead of as a 0-1 relative scale.
notes: The table contains only relative 0-1 SUPPLY and DEMAND series, so all units are relative. Price and protest mentions are narration-only and should not be given table-derived numbers.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
